conventions.convention: The background is R⁴ with the identity inertial chart, η = diag(-1,1,1,1), and time orientation ∂₀. First-order indices are raised and lowered with η; Box = -∂₀² + ∂₁² + ∂₂² + ∂₃².
The standard phase is u = x⁰ - x³, du = (1,0,0,-1), T = ∂₀ + ∂₃, and k = -ω du = ω η(T,·). A single-frequency plane wave requires k ≠ 0; ω = 0 is excluded from that null-wave classification.

An observer n is future unit timelike, and a propagation direction s is unit spacelike and orthogonal to n. The screen is {v : η(v,n) = η(v,s) = 0}; its rank-two projector is p = I + n⊗n-flat - s⊗s-flat. TT projection subtracts one half of the screen trace, rather than the rest-space trace.
Gauge transformation means h′ab = hab - ∂aξb - ∂bξa within the fixed background chart. Harmonic gauge is ∂a bar-hab = 0; it is not a change of chart.
R(X,Y)Z = ∇X∇YZ - ∇Y∇XZ - ∇[X,Y]Z, with R(∂c,∂d)∂b = Rᵃbcd∂a. Geodesic deviation consequently has sign D²J = R(T,J)T.

In SI length coordinates x⁰ = ct, all coordinates have units metres, metric perturbation components and λ are dimensionless, curvature components have units m⁻², and the angular frequency associated with ω is c|ω|.

The physical residual functional uses inverse powers of L multiplying first and second coordinate derivatives, evaluated as fixed SI numerical chart values. The threshold is δ₀ = 1/16. These are numerical controls, not intrinsic norms or observables; compact sets in these clauses are nonempty.

Detector length is the metric length of the prescribed chart-straight spatial segment at equal chart time, with δ ≠ 0. Strain is Lδ/|δ| - 1. It is neither shortest spatial distance nor optical readout; infinitesimal relative acceleration is distinct from finite-pair acceleration.

Physical conclusions are conditional model deductions with no empirical premises. A quadratic exact-vacuum residual is not an exact vacuum solution. Physical body histories may be restrictions of maximal mathematical geodesics.

load_bearing.statement: For a nonzero null covector k and a chosen adapted observer and propagation direction, the harmonic-gauge amplitude space satisfies V₀ = T ⊕ G, dim G = 4, dim T = 2 and dim V₀ = 6. Every X ∈ V₀ has exactly one pure plane-wave gauge subtraction yielding a TT representative; V₀/G is isomorphic to T.

For bounded smooth profiles A₊, A× on R and the stated TT planar perturbation, η + λh is Lorentzian on R⁴ when M > 0 and |λ| < 1/(2M), with the zero-profile case trivial. The perturbation is traceless, in harmonic gauge, satisfies Box bar-h = 0 and G⁽¹⁾(h) = 0, and has the stated quadratic Einstein-tensor residual on every nonempty compact set for sufficiently small |λ|.

For a flat linearized family, R⁽¹⁾abcd = ½(∂b∂c had + ∂a∂d hbc - ∂a∂c hbd - ∂b∂d hac), and this coefficient is unchanged by smooth gauge transformations. For spatial planar profiles, R⁽¹⁾0i0j = -½F″ij and R⁽¹⁾ⁱ00j = +½F″ⁱj. Its η-contraction is the linearized Ricci coefficient, which vanishes for TT planar perturbations.

For the stated smooth metric and stress-energy families satisfying the adopted field law for every λ, differentiation gives G⁽¹⁾ab(h) + Λhab = κT⁽¹⁾ab. In the source-free Λ = 0 branch, harmonic gauge gives Box bar-h = 0. Clause (d) separately bounds the exact vacuum residual of a perturbation satisfying G⁽¹⁾(h) = 0 on a nonempty compact set under |λ|B_K(h) ≤ 1/16. Clause (e) assumes countable choice for all-space harmonic-gauge existence.

The screen and spatial projectors have ranks two and three. The TT projection is idempotent with image exactly the two-dimensional TT tensor space; restricted to spatial symmetric tensors, it is the orthogonal projection for the stated positive definite inner product.

For the specified TT datum and detector curves, the finite arm path is σs(q) = (cs,x₀ + qδ), q ∈ [0,1]. Where its radicand is positive, Lδ(s) = |δ|∫₀¹√(1 + λaδ(s,q)) dq and Sδ(s) = Lδ(s)/|δ| - 1, with aδ = δⁱδʲhij/|δ|².

concerns.concern: The first Remark states the trace identity 'For a projector q of rank r' without requiring η-self-adjointness. It is false for a general idempotent. In the standard chart, let q have spatial block [[1,1,0],[0,0,0],[0,0,1]] and zero time row/column, and take A = diag(0,0,1,0). Then q² = q and rank q = 2, but q^{cd}A_cd = 0 while the projected tensor has trace 1. The identity therefore needs an orthogonal-projector hypothesis. This does not invalidate the proved formulas for p and h.

Statement (a) writes 'h-p=s-flat⊗s', whereas its immediately following component formula hᵃ_b-pᵃ_b=sᵃs_b describes s⊗s-flat. The tensor-factor order is reversed. The same item's first Remark also mentions a 'four-dimensional rest-space projector in a curved model', although the framework's four-dimensional Lorentzian model has three-dimensional observer rest spaces.

Statement (a), [L1] and proof 1.1 use η(n,k), η(k,k) and η(k,n) with k declared to be a covector, although η is a bilinear form on vectors. The intended quantities k(n) and η⁻¹(k,k) are recoverable from the following musical-isomorphism formula, but the mixed pairing notation is not defined.

The final Remark repeats the general trace identity 'for a projector q of rank r' without an orthogonality hypothesis. For q with spatial block [[1,1,0],[0,0,0],[0,0,1]], zero time row/column, and A = diag(0,0,1,0), q is a rank-two idempotent, q^{cd}A_cd = 0, but the displayed projected tensor has trace 1. The particular counterexample using the orthogonal spatial projector is correct; the generalized remark is overstrong.

alerts.finding: Definition (c) permits any open interval J₀ with nonempty interior, then defines the variation field 'along the curve s↦F(0,s)'. It does not require 0 ∈ J₀, so taking J₀ = (1,2) makes that curve undefined. It also writes s↦∂rF(r,s) without evaluating r at 0; for general r this lies in T_{F(r,s)}M rather than T_{F(0,s)}M. The base parameter and evaluation must be specified.

Proof step 5.1 reads 'Define G(x,t,v):=H_{F(·,v)}(x,t-v). From the defining integral,' and immediately ends with justification tags. It contains no derivation of the Duhamel solution, zero initial data, forcing equation or compact derivative bounds asserted in clause (b). These are routine moving-endpoint differentiation and compactness arguments, but the actual supplier step is unfinished.
